text:
The Ducks were two goals down in the first period, and they did not stay there. Anaheim erased a 2-0 Philadelphia lead and beat the Flyers 5-4, ending a five-game winless run (0-5-0) and ending Philadelphia's three-game winning streak. Tristan Luneau, a second-round pick in 2022 who piled up 83 points in 65 junior games for Gatineau, scored what proved the go-ahead goal early in the third, on a shot the model gave a 2% chance. He added two assists.

The Flyers scored twice on the power play in the first period, from Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone, and they led for most of the opening 40 minutes. Then the second period turned. Anaheim out-chanced Philadelphia 2.22 to 0.65 in expected goals, which measures the quality of the chances a team creates. Leo Carlsson, the 2023 No. 2 pick, tied things up in the middle of that stretch, and A.J. Greer and Judd Caulfield scored too. Tyson Foerster's shorthanded goal gave the Flyers a brief 3-2 lead, but Caulfield tied it 3-3 about a minute later.

Across the full game the play was close at even strength (1.83 expected goals for ANA, 1.89 for PHI), and Anaheim's edge came from that second period and its power play. By the numbers, the Ducks deserved to win 67% of the time, meaning they won that share of simulated replays of every shot. Beckett Sennecke made it 5-3 on the power play, and Michkov answered with his second goal just over a minute later, but Philadelphia could not find a fifth. Anaheim leaves with a win that breaks its slide, and Philadelphia with a loss that stops its run at three.
